title: Panama: a canal climbs
hook: Does a ship simply sail through at sea level?

predict.question: How does the canal cross its inland section?
options: Locks lift ships to a lake

frames.heading: Atlantic entrance
frames.text: A ship approaches the Atlantic locks.

frames.heading: Gatun locks
frames.text: Locks lift the ship toward Gatun Lake.

frames.heading: Lake crossing
frames.text: The ship crosses the elevated lake.

frames.heading: Pacific descent
frames.text: Locks lower the ship toward the Pacific.

reveal: Panama is a lock canal, not a sea-level trench. Ships are raised to Gatun Lake, about 26 meters above sea level, and lowered again on the other side. The canal opened in 1914. These steps explain the system rather than reconstructing one named ship’s exact passage.
limit: Opening-era process diagram; generalized canal geometry, not a ship log.

sources.section: Lock system, Gatun Lake elevation and Atlantic/Pacific locks
